civics.emerged: ~1,854 CE Northcote–Trevelyan report; ~1,883 CE Pendleton Act

capabilities: officials are recruited by open competitive examination and hold office during good behaviour

civics.name: Nationalism
civics.desc: The nation, defined by language and history, is held to be the proper unit of the state.
civics.emerged: ~1,789 CE French nation in arms; ~1,807 CE Addresses to the German Nation

capabilities: the nation, defined by language and history, is held to be the proper unit of the state

civics.name: Nature conservation
civics.desc: Land is set aside to protect landscapes, species and their habitats.
civics.emerged: ~1,872 CE Yellowstone National Park

capabilities: land is set aside to protect landscapes, species and their habitats

civics.name: Popular sovereignty
civics.desc: Sovereignty is held to belong to the nation, exercised through its representatives.
civics.emerged: ~1,776 CE Declaration of Independence; ~1,789 CE Declaration of the Rights of Man

capabilities: sovereignty is held to belong to the nation, exercised through its representatives

civics.name: Freedom of the press
civics.desc: Prior censorship is abolished; printers answer only to the courts afterwards.
civics.emerged: ~1,766 CE Swedish Freedom of the Press Act

capabilities: prior censorship is abolished; printers answer only to the courts afterwards

civics.name: Professional sport
civics.desc: Paid teams play in national leagues followed by mass audiences.
civics.emerged: ~1,876 CE baseball's National League; ~1,888 CE Football League

capabilities: paid teams play in national leagues followed by mass audiences

civics.name: Public postal service
civics.desc: The state carries anyone's letters at a uniform prepaid rate.
civics.emerged: ~1,840 CE Penny Post

capabilities: the state carries anyone's letters at a uniform prepaid rate

civics.name: Referendum
civics.desc: Voters decide laws directly at the ballot box.
civics.emerged: ~1,874 CE Swiss optional referendum

capabilities: voters decide laws directly at the ballot box

civics.name: Research university
civics.desc: Universities pay professors to research as well as teach and train doctoral students.
civics.emerged: ~1,810 CE University of Berlin

capabilities: universities pay professors to research as well as teach and train doctoral students

civics.name: Secret ballot
civics.desc: Votes are cast in private on official ballots.
civics.emerged: ~1,856 CE Victoria (Australia)

capabilities: votes are cast in private on official ballots

civics.name: Secular state
civics.desc: The state recognizes no official church and treats every faith alike in law.
civics.emerged: ~1,791 CE First Amendment; ~1,905 CE French separation law

capabilities: the state recognizes no official church and treats every faith alike in law

civics.name: Settler land grants
civics.desc: Public land is surveyed and granted to settlers who farm it.
civics.emerged: ~1,862 CE Homestead Act

capabilities: public land is surveyed and granted to settlers who farm it

civics.name: Socialism
civics.desc: Workers' movements demand collective ownership and an end to class exploitation.
civics.emerged: ~1,825 CE Owenite communities; ~1,848 CE Communist Manifesto

capabilities: workers' movements demand collective ownership and an end to class exploitation

civics.name: Women's suffrage
civics.desc: Women gain the vote on the same terms as men.
civics.emerged: ~1,893 CE New Zealand

capabilities: women gain the vote on the same terms as men

civics.name: Revolutionary republic
civics.desc: A republic founded by revolution in the name of the people, with a citizen army and emergency committees.
civics.emerged: ~1,792 CE French First Republic

capabilities: a republic founded by revolution in the name of the people, with a citizen army and emergency committees

civics.name: Arms control
civics.desc: States cap and verify their weapons by treaty.
civics.emerged: ~1,968 CE Non-Proliferation Treaty; ~1,972 CE SALT I

capabilities: states cap and verify their weapons by treaty

civics.name: Civil rights law
civics.desc: Law forbids discrimination by race, religion or sex in public life and work.
civics.emerged: ~1,964 CE Civil Rights Act

capabilities: law forbids discrimination by race, religion or sex in public life and work

civics.name: Climate accords
civics.desc: States negotiate shared limits on greenhouse emissions.
civics.emerged: ~1,992 CE UN Framework Convention on Climate Change

capabilities: states negotiate shared limits on greenhouse emissions

civics.name: Collective security
civics.desc: Members pledge to act together against an aggressor.
civics.emerged: ~1,919 CE League of Nations; ~1,945 CE UN Charter

capabilities: members pledge to act together against an aggressor

civics.name: Data protection law
civics.desc: Law limits how states and firms collect and use personal records.
civics.emerged: ~1,970 CE Hesse data protection act

capabilities: law limits how states and firms collect and use personal records

civics.name: Decolonization
civics.desc: Colonies win independence under a doctrine of self-determination of peoples.
civics.emerged: ~1,947 CE Indian independence; ~1,960 CE UN Resolution 1514

capabilities: colonies win independence under a doctrine of self-determination of peoples

civics.name: Environmental regulation
civics.desc: Agencies limit pollution of air, water and soil by permit and standard.
civics.emerged: ~1,970 CE US Environmental Protection Agency

capabilities: agencies limit pollution of air, water and soil by permit and standard

civics.name: Fascism
civics.desc: An ultranationalist mass movement seeks a single-party state built on mobilization and violence.
civics.emerged: ~1,919 CE Fasci di Combattimento

capabilities: an ultranationalist mass movement seeks a single-party state built on mobilization and violence

civics.name: Human rights law
civics.desc: Rights are declared to belong to every person and are monitored internationally.
civics.emerged: ~1,948 CE Universal Declaration of Human Rights

capabilities: rights are declared to belong to every person and are monitored internationally

civics.name: Integrated alliance command
civics.desc: Allies place forces under a joint peacetime command.
civics.emerged: ~1,949 CE North Atlantic Treaty; ~1,951 CE SHAPE

capabilities: allies place forces under a joint peacetime command

future.system: Politics / Diplomacy - alliances
future.description: allies place forces under a joint peacetime command

future.system: Battle Layer - joint command of formations
future.description: allied formations act under one command

civics.name: International tribunals
civics.desc: International courts try individuals for war crimes and crimes against humanity.
civics.emerged: ~1,945 CE Nuremberg tribunal; ~2,002 CE International Criminal Court

capabilities: international courts try individuals for war crimes and crimes against humanity

civics.name: Internet governance
civics.desc: Shared bodies and national regulators set rules for a global network.
civics.emerged: ~1,998 CE ICANN

capabilities: shared bodies and national regulators set rules for a global network

civics.name: Multilateral trade rules
civics.desc: Many states bind their tariffs and settle trade disputes under shared rules.
civics.emerged: ~1,947 CE General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade

capabilities: many states bind their tariffs and settle trade disputes under shared rules

civics.name: Nuclear deterrence doctrine
civics.desc: War is to be prevented by the threat of nuclear retaliation.
civics.emerged: ~1,954 CE massive retaliation doctrine

capabilities: war is to be prevented by the threat of nuclear retaliation

civics.name: Public broadcasting
civics.desc: A licensed public body runs national radio and later television.
civics.emerged: ~1,927 CE British Broadcasting Corporation charter

capabilities: a licensed public body runs national radio and later television

civics.name: Science policy
civics.desc: The state funds research through grant agencies and sets national research priorities.
civics.emerged: ~1,945 CE Science, the Endless Frontier; ~1,950 CE US National Science Foundation

capabilities: the state funds research through grant agencies and sets national research priorities

civics.name: State propaganda
civics.desc: A government office shapes news, films and broadcasts to mobilize opinion.
civics.emerged: ~1,917 CE US Committee on Public Information; ~1,933 CE German propaganda ministry

capabilities: a government office shapes news, films and broadcasts to mobilize opinion

civics.name: Total mobilization
civics.desc: The whole economy and manpower of the state are directed to war.
civics.emerged: ~1,914 CE general mobilization

capabilities: the whole economy and manpower of the state are directed to war

civics.name: Zoning
civics.desc: Cities divide land into zones with permitted uses and building envelopes.
civics.emerged: ~1,916 CE New York zoning resolution

capabilities: cities divide land into zones with permitted uses and building envelopes

civics.name: Fascist state
civics.desc: A one-party state of an ultranationalist movement under a leader, mobilizing society through propaganda and corporations.
civics.emerged: ~1,922 CE Italy; ~1,933 CE Germany

capabilities: a one-party state of an ultranationalist movement under a leader, mobilizing society through propaganda and corporations

civics.name: Burial of the dead
civics.desc: The band buries its dead with ochre and ornaments and mourns them together, binding the living to one another and to the places where their kin lie.
civics.emerged: ~100 kya Qafzeh and Skhul burials with ochre; ~34 kya Sungir grave goods

capabilities: The band buries its dead with ochre and ornaments and mourns them together, binding the living to one another and to the places where their kin lie.

civics.name: Guest right
civics.desc: Strangers who come in peace are fed and protected for a time, so people can cross other bands' land to trade, marry or resettle without being treated as raiders.
civics.emerged: ~40 kya inferred from shell beads exchanged across band territories; universal in recorded foragers

capabilities: Strangers who come in peace are fed and protected for a time, so people can cross other bands' land to trade, marry or resettle without being treated as raiders.

civics.name: Initiation of the young
civics.desc: At puberty boys and girls are secluded with elders, taught the band's tracking, plant and animal lore and its rules, and come back as adults.
civics.emerged: ~15 kya adolescent footprints in the deep chambers of Tuc d'Audoubert and Niaux (initiation is one reading); initiation of youths is recorded in nearly every Australian and African forager society

capabilities: At puberty boys and girls are secluded with elders, taught the band's tracking, plant and animal lore and its rules, and come back as adults.

civics.name: Fire-stick land management
civics.desc: The band burns country in small patches at chosen seasons, opening grassland that draws game and renews food plants.
civics.emerged: ~45 kya change in Sahul fire regimes (contested); recorded Aboriginal mosaic burning

capabilities: The band burns country in small patches at chosen seasons, opening grassland that draws game and renews food plants.

civics.name: Seasonal round
civics.desc: The band moves between known camps on a fixed yearly schedule, reaching fish runs, nut groves and herds when each is at its best.
civics.emerged: ~23 kya Ohalo II (Sea of Galilee): brush huts reoccupied season after season

capabilities: The band moves between known camps on a fixed yearly schedule, reaching fish runs, nut groves and herds when each is at its best.

civics.name: Wayfinding lore
civics.desc: Bands memorise routes, landmarks, water holes and star rises in song and story, so a party can travel far beyond its home range and find its way back.
civics.emerged: ~40 kya inferred from raw materials carried hundreds of km; ethnographic route songs (songlines)

capabilities: Bands memorise routes, landmarks, water holes and star rises in song and story, so a party can travel far beyond its home range and find its way back.

civics.name: Division of labour by sex and age
civics.desc: Men hunt large game far from camp while women, children and elders gather plants, trap small animals and process food. Each household draws on both.
civics.emerged: ~30 kya Upper Palaeolithic: plant grinding (Bilancino, Pavlov) beside specialised projectile hunting; Kuhn and Stiner (2006) argue a sexual division of foraging work arose with modern humans

capabilities: Men hunt large game far from camp while women, children and elders gather plants, trap small animals and process food. Each household draws on both.

civics.name: Band territories
civics.desc: Each band holds a known range. In a lean season its members may forage on a neighbour's land by asking leave through kin and exchange partners.
civics.emerged: ~40-30 kya regional ornament styles marking group areas in Aurignacian Europe (Vanhaeren and d'Errico); access by kin permission in forager ethnography (Ju/'hoansi n!ore)

capabilities: Each band holds a known range. In a lean season its members may forage on a neighbour's land by asking leave through kin and exchange partners.

civics.name: Customary sanctions
civics.desc: Ridicule, shunning and, at the last, expulsion from the band keep bullies and shirkers in line. Everyone knows the rules because everyone tells them.
civics.emerged: ~40 kya and earlier (inferred from forager ethnography: ridicule, shunning and expulsion; no direct date)

capabilities: Ridicule, shunning and, at the last, expulsion from the band keep bullies and shirkers in line. Everyone knows the rules because everyone tells them.

civics.name: Prestige leadership
civics.desc: Some men and women lead by skill and generosity rather than birth: others follow them on the hunt, in moves and in disputes, but can leave them at will.
civics.emerged: ~10 kya and earlier: ethnographic headmen whose influence rests on generosity and skill (inferred for late foragers)

capabilities: Some men and women lead by skill and generosity rather than birth: others follow them on the hunt, in moves and in disputes, but can leave them at will.

civics.name: Hunt leaders
civics.desc: For the great autumn drive the bands choose a leader whose orders bind everyone; anyone who startles the herd early is punished. After the kill and drying of meat his authority lapses.
civics.emerged: ~20 kya Amvrosievka (Ukraine) bison drive-and-kill site and Solutré horse kills; Plains 'buffalo police' who commanded the communal hunt recorded ethnographically

capabilities: For the great autumn drive the bands choose a leader whose orders bind everyone; anyone who startles the herd early is punished. After the kill and drying of meat his authority lapses.

civics.name: Seasonal gatherings
civics.desc: Several bands meet at a rich place each year to feast, trade, arrange marriages and settle quarrels between groups, then disperse again.
civics.emerged: ~17 kya Magdalenian aggregation sites inferred in Cantabria (Conkey on Altamira); ethnographic analogy with seasonal camps of many bands

capabilities: Several bands meet at a rich place each year to feast, trade, arrange marriages and settle quarrels between groups, then disperse again.

civics.name: Food-sharing norms
civics.desc: Whoever brings in meat must share it with the whole band. A hunter's bad week no longer starves his children, and no family hoards while others go hungry.
civics.emerged: ~100 kya and earlier: shared butchery at hearths; demand-sharing universal among recorded foragers

capabilities: Whoever brings in meat must share it with the whole band. A hunter's bad week no longer starves his children, and no family hoards while others go hungry.

civics.name: Out-marriage between bands
civics.desc: Young people must marry outside their own band. Every family then has in-laws in other bands, and when its own country fails it can go and live with them.
civics.emerged: ~34 kya Sunghir (Russia): genomes of the buried show no close inbreeding, so mates came from a wide network; out-marriage is near-universal among recorded foragers

capabilities: Young people must marry outside their own band. Every family then has in-laws in other bands, and when its own country fails it can go and live with them.

civics.name: Monumental shrines
civics.desc: Communities raise stone enclosures and tombs too large for any household, feeding the work parties with feasts and gathering at them for rites.
civics.emerged: ~9,500 BCE Göbekli Tepe enclosures; ~3,000 BCE Stonehenge

capabilities: Communities raise stone enclosures and tombs too large for any household, feeding the work parties with feasts and gathering at them for rites.

civics.name: Barter of staples
civics.desc: Villagers trade surplus grain, salt and stone with neighbours at agreed equivalents, without waiting for a gift to be returned.
civics.emerged: ~7,000 BCE obsidian, shell and grain exchanged between Anatolian and Levantine villages

capabilities: Villagers trade surplus grain, salt and stone with neighbours at agreed equivalents, without waiting for a gift to be returned.

civics.name: Craft specialization
civics.desc: Some households work part-time as potters, bead-makers or smiths and exchange their wares for food.
civics.emerged: ~6,000 BCE Halaf workshop pottery; ~4,500 BCE Varna goldsmiths

capabilities: Some households work part-time as potters, bead-makers or smiths and exchange their wares for food.

civics.name: Stock friendship
civics.desc: A herder places some of his animals with bond-friends in other districts and keeps theirs in return, so drought or disease never takes his whole herd.
civics.emerged: ~4,500 BCE inferred with the spread of herding into the Sahara and East Africa (ethnographic analogy); bond-friends who keep each other's cattle recorded among the Turkana, Jie and Maasai

capabilities: A herder places some of his animals with bond-friends in other districts and keeps theirs in return, so drought or disease never takes his whole herd.

civics.name: Fishing-station rights
civics.desc: A kin group owns a named weir or fishing place and keeps it in repair. Others fish there only by its leave, so the weir is worth rebuilding every year.
civics.emerged: ~6,000 BCE Mesolithic fish weirs on the Liffey (Dublin) rebuilt on the same spot for centuries; kin-owned fishing stations recorded on the Northwest Coast

capabilities: A kin group owns a named weir or fishing place and keeps it in repair. Others fish there only by its leave, so the weir is worth rebuilding every year.

civics.name: Inviolable seed corn
civics.desc: Next year's seed is set aside at harvest and may not be eaten even in hunger. The best ears are kept for it, so every planting starts from good seed.
civics.emerged: ~9,500 BCE purpose-built grain stores at Jerf el-Ahmar and Dhra'; keeping seed back from eating is the precondition of domestication, and peasant custom treats it as untouchable

capabilities: Next year's seed is set aside at harvest and may not be eaten even in hunger. The best ears are kept for it, so every planting starts from good seed.

civics.name: Transhumance
civics.desc: Herders move flocks between summer mountain pastures and winter lowlands along customary routes, so neither range is grazed bare.
civics.emerged: ~5,000 BCE seasonal herd movement in the Zagros and the Alps (isotopic evidence)

capabilities: Herders move flocks between summer mountain pastures and winter lowlands along customary routes, so neither range is grazed bare.

civics.name: Island colonization voyages
civics.desc: Settlers sail to islands with seed, breeding stock and supplies to found new communities beyond sight of land.
civics.emerged: ~8,500 BCE farmers reach Cyprus with goats, pigs and cattle; ~7,000 BCE Crete settled

capabilities: Settlers sail to islands with seed, breeding stock and supplies to found new communities beyond sight of land.

civics.name: Daughter villages
civics.desc: When a village grows too large, a group of households leaves with seed and stock to found a new village nearby.
civics.emerged: ~7,000 BCE farming villages spread into Greece; ~5,500 BCE Linearbandkeramik spread across central Europe

capabilities: When a village grows too large, a group of households leaves with seed and stock to found a new village nearby.

civics.name: Reciprocal work parties
civics.desc: Households call on neighbours to raise houses and bring in harvests, repaying with food, drink and labour in turn.
civics.emerged: ~7,400 BCE Çatalhöyük houses rebuilt in place by neighbouring households (inferred)

capabilities: Households call on neighbours to raise houses and bring in harvests, repaying with food, drink and labour in turn.

civics.name: Compensation for injury
civics.desc: A killing or injury is settled by a fixed payment from the offender's kin to the victim's, set by the elders, instead of by revenge.
civics.emerged: pre-literate practice (ethnographic analogy: payments in livestock and valuables); first written ~2,100 BCE in the laws of Ur-Nammu (silver for injuries)

capabilities: A killing or injury is settled by a fixed payment from the offender's kin to the victim's, set by the elders, instead of by revenge.

civics.name: Rights of clearance
civics.desc: Whoever clears a plot from the forest holds it while he crops it. When it is left to regrow it returns to the lineage, and any member may clear it again.
civics.emerged: ~5,500 BCE inferred for early farmers clearing the European forest; recorded among swidden farmers of Africa, Southeast Asia and Amazonia (the clearer holds the plot while it is cropped)

capabilities: Whoever clears a plot from the forest holds it while he crops it. When it is left to regrow it returns to the lineage, and any member may clear it again.

civics.name: Household fields
civics.desc: Each household works its own fields within marked boundaries and passes them to its heirs; the village recognizes the holding.
civics.emerged: ~3,700 BCE Ceide Fields (Ireland), a stone-walled field system of separate holdings

capabilities: Each household works its own fields within marked boundaries and passes them to its heirs; the village recognizes the holding.

civics.name: Witnessed agreements
civics.desc: A sale, loan or pledge is made before named witnesses who can later swear to its terms, so a deal with a stranger can be enforced.
civics.emerged: pre-literate practice; witness lists on Sumerian land-sale contracts by ~2,600 BCE (Fara)

capabilities: A sale, loan or pledge is made before named witnesses who can later swear to its terms, so a deal with a stranger can be enforced.

civics.name: First-comer precedence
civics.desc: The lineage descended from the first settlers keeps the shrine of the land and allots fields to later arrivals, who farm by its leave.
civics.emerged: ~7,000 BCE Çatalhöyük house continuity over many generations (inferred); ethnographic earth-priest lineages of West Africa

capabilities: The lineage descended from the first settlers keeps the shrine of the land and allots fields to later arrivals, who farm by its leave.

civics.name: Insignia of rank
civics.desc: Sceptres, maces and gold ornaments mark who holds rank, so authority is recognized by people who have never met its holder.
civics.emerged: ~4,500 BCE Varna gold sceptre and ornaments; ~3,500 BCE Nahal Mishmar copper maceheads

capabilities: Sceptres, maces and gold ornaments mark who holds rank, so authority is recognized by people who have never met its holder.

civics.name: Age sets
civics.desc: Youths initiated together form a set for life. The set serves as warriors guarding herds and camps, then rises together to married men and to ruling elders.
civics.emerged: ~3,000 BCE inferred with the East African pastoral Neolithic (ethnographic analogy); recorded among the Maasai and Nuer and in the Oromo gada system

capabilities: Youths initiated together form a set for life. The set serves as warriors guarding herds and camps, then rises together to married men and to ruling elders.

civics.name: Warrior retinues
civics.desc: A chief keeps armed followers who are fed from his hall and fight at his call, and who also collect what is owed to him.
civics.emerged: ~4,500 BCE weapon-rich graves at Varna; ~2,800 BCE Corded Ware battle-axe burials

capabilities: A chief keeps armed followers who are fed from his hall and fight at his call, and who also collect what is owed to him.

civics.name: Village defences
civics.desc: The village digs ditches, raises a wall or palisade and keeps a watch, so raiders cannot simply carry off the stored harvest.
civics.emerged: ~8,000 BCE wall and tower at Jericho; ~5,000 BCE ditched and palisaded villages in central Europe

capabilities: The village digs ditches, raises a wall or palisade and keeps a watch, so raiders cannot simply carry off the stored harvest.

civics.name: Big-man polity
civics.desc: Leaders compete for followers by sponsoring feasts and exchanges; their authority lasts only as long as their generosity and is not inherited.
civics.emerged: ~6,500 BCE early Neolithic villages (inferred from feasting debris); ethnographic Melanesian big-men

capabilities: Leaders compete for followers by sponsoring feasts and exchanges; their authority lasts only as long as their generosity and is not inherited.

civics.name: Segmentary lineage society
civics.desc: Lineages unite against outsiders and split when they grow, with no permanent chief; elders of each segment settle disputes.
civics.emerged: ~6,000 BCE Neolithic lineage villages (inferred); ethnographic Nuer and Tiv

capabilities: Lineages unite against outsiders and split when they grow, with no permanent chief; elders of each segment settle disputes.

civics.name: Sodalities
civics.desc: Men's and women's societies recruit across lineages and villages. Members keep a lodge, hold rites and police camps, and a member is received by his society in any village where it meets.
civics.emerged: ~9,500 BCE Göbekli Tepe and ~8,000 BCE Nevalı Çori enclosures, read by their excavators as meeting places of cult societies (interpretation); kiva societies and Plains soldier societies recorded ethnographically

capabilities: Men's and women's societies recruit across lineages and villages. Members keep a lodge, hold rites and police camps, and a member is received by his society in any village where it meets.

civics.name: Village headship
civics.desc: One household head is acknowledged as the village's head: he speaks for it to outsiders and calls the households to common work.
civics.emerged: ~5,500 BCE Ubaid villages with a larger central house (inferred leadership); ethnographic analogy with village headmen

capabilities: One household head is acknowledged as the village's head: he speaks for it to outsiders and calls the households to common work.

civics.name: Bridewealth
civics.desc: The groom's kin give livestock to the bride's kin. The payment makes the marriage and gives the children to the father's lineage, which must then feed and protect them.
civics.emerged: ~6,000 BCE inferred with cattle and sheep herding (ethnographic analogy: Nuer cattle, Zulu lobola); first written as terhatum in the Laws of Eshnunna ~1,800 BCE

capabilities: The groom's kin give livestock to the bride's kin. The payment makes the marriage and gives the children to the father's lineage, which must then feed and protect them.

civics.name: Communal storehouses
civics.desc: The village keeps its grain in common storehouses under agreed rules, so a household with a poor crop can draw on the common stock.
civics.emerged: ~9,300 BCE Dhra' (Jordan): free-standing granaries shared by the settlement

capabilities: The village keeps its grain in common storehouses under agreed rules, so a household with a poor crop can draw on the common stock.

civics.name: Extended-family households
civics.desc: Parents, married sons or daughters and their children live in one long house under its senior couple, sharing hearths, stores and labour.
civics.emerged: ~5,500 BCE LBK longhouses up to 40 m long, each housing several related couples; matrilineal longhouses recorded among the Iroquois

capabilities: Parents, married sons or daughters and their children live in one long house under its senior couple, sharing hearths, stores and labour.

civics.name: Epic literature
civics.desc: Heroic tales once sung are written down, copied in the schools and recited at court and festival.
civics.emerged: ~2,100 BCE Sumerian Gilgamesh poems; ~1,800 BCE Old Babylonian Gilgamesh epic

capabilities: Heroic tales once sung are written down, copied in the schools and recited at court and festival.

civics.name: State pantheon
civics.desc: The city gods are arranged in one ranked family under a high god, whose shrine confers kingship over all the cities.
civics.emerged: ~2,600 BCE Fara god lists; ~2,100 BCE Nippur as the seat of Enlil, who confers kingship

capabilities: The city gods are arranged in one ranked family under a high god, whose shrine confers kingship over all the cities.

civics.name: Interest-bearing loans
civics.desc: Temples and merchants lend barley and silver at fixed interest, recorded on sealed tablets, to finance seed and caravans.
civics.emerged: ~2,400 BCE Lagash barley and silver loans at interest; ~1,754 BCE Hammurabi fixes the rates

capabilities: Temples and merchants lend barley and silver at fixed interest, recorded on sealed tablets, to finance seed and caravans.

civics.name: Investment partnerships
civics.desc: Several investors pool gold in one 'bag' entrusted to a travelling merchant for years. He trades with it, they share the profit, and the capital stays at work between caravans.
civics.emerged: ~1,900 BCE Kanesh (Kültepe) tablets: Old Assyrian naruqqum 'money-bag' partnerships, investors pooling gold for a merchant for ten years or more

capabilities: Several investors pool gold in one 'bag' entrusted to a travelling merchant for years. He trades with it, they share the profit, and the capital stays at work between caravans.

civics.name: Court upbringing of vassal heirs
civics.desc: Sons of subject kings are brought to the great king's palace, schooled with his own children and sent back to rule when their fathers die.
civics.emerged: ~1,450 BCE Thutmose III brings the sons of Levantine rulers to be raised in the Egyptian royal nursery (kap) and sends them home as vassal kings

capabilities: Sons of subject kings are brought to the great king's palace, schooled with his own children and sent back to rule when their fathers die.

civics.name: Frontier fortresses
civics.desc: A chain of forts with commandants and scribes holds a frontier, controls crossings and reports movements to the capital.
civics.emerged: ~1,860 BCE Middle Kingdom forts at the Second Cataract; ~1,800 BCE Semna despatches

capabilities: A chain of forts with commandants and scribes holds a frontier, controls crossings and reports movements to the capital.

civics.name: Royal expeditions
civics.desc: The crown sends organised expeditions to distant lands for incense, gold and stone, and records what they find.
civics.emerged: ~2,450 BCE Sahure's voyage to Punt; ~1,470 BCE Hatshepsut's Punt expedition

capabilities: The crown sends organised expeditions to distant lands for incense, gold and stone, and records what they find.

civics.name: Victory stelae
civics.desc: Kings set up carved and inscribed stones at frontiers and city gates announcing their victories and warning rebels.
civics.emerged: ~2,250 BCE Naram-Sin victory stele; ~1,850 BCE Senusret III boundary stelae at Semna

capabilities: Kings set up carved and inscribed stones at frontiers and city gates announcing their victories and warning rebels.

civics.name: Herding contracts
civics.desc: Temple and palace flocks are entrusted to herdsmen under contract: a fixed number of lambs and weight of wool per hundred ewes, an allowance for losses, and the surplus is theirs.
civics.emerged: ~2,050 BCE Ur III herding accounts fix lambing and wool quotas for temple flocks; Laws of Hammurabi §261-267 (~1,754 BCE) regulate hired herdsmen

capabilities: Temple and palace flocks are entrusted to herdsmen under contract: a fixed number of lambs and weight of wool per hundred ewes, an allowance for losses, and the surplus is theirs.

civics.name: Wage and hire tariffs
civics.desc: The law fixes what a harvester, an ox-team or a boat earns for a day's hire, so workers can be hired without haggling.
civics.emerged: ~1,800 BCE Laws of Eshnunna fix harvesters' wages and the hire of oxen and boats

capabilities: The law fixes what a harvester, an ox-team or a boat earns for a day's hire, so workers can be hired without haggling.

civics.name: Merchant colony courts
civics.desc: Merchants abroad form a colony with its own court; disputes over debts and lost goods are settled on the spot under the home city's law.
civics.emerged: ~1,900 BCE Old Assyrian karum at Kanesh deciding merchants' disputes

capabilities: Merchants abroad form a colony with its own court; disputes over debts and lost goods are settled on the spot under the home city's law.

civics.name: Judges and court records
civics.desc: Appointed judges hear cases, take witnesses' oaths and record the verdict on a tablet, so a decided case stays decided.
civics.emerged: ~2,100 BCE Ur III ditilla records of completed lawsuits; ~1,754 BCE judges in Hammurabi's laws

capabilities: Appointed judges hear cases, take witnesses' oaths and record the verdict on a tablet, so a decided case stays decided.

civics.name: Campaign supply depots
civics.desc: Officials stock grain, fodder and weapons at stations along the march so an army can campaign far from home.
civics.emerged: ~1,457 BCE Thutmose III stocks Phoenician harbours before his campaigns; ~720 BCE Assyrian road-station stores

capabilities: Officials stock grain, fodder and weapons at stations along the march so an army can campaign far from home.

civics.name: Royal road-houses
civics.desc: The crown builds staffed rest-houses a day's march apart on the main roads, with water, fodder and food for official travellers and caravans.
civics.emerged: ~2,090 BCE Shulgi of Ur claims to have built road-houses with gardens and wells along the highways; Ur III way-station accounts record rations to travellers

capabilities: The crown builds staffed rest-houses a day's march apart on the main roads, with water, fodder and food for official travellers and caravans.

civics.name: Overkingship
civics.desc: A great king rules other kings, who keep their thrones in return for oaths, tribute and troops.
civics.emerged: ~2,400 BCE Ebla's sworn overlordship of Abarsal; ~1,350 BCE Hittite vassal treaties

capabilities: A great king rules other kings, who keep their thrones in return for oaths, tribute and troops.

civics.name: Village and ward heads
civics.desc: A head chosen in the village or city ward answers to the palace for its dues, labour levies and crimes, and speaks for it before officials.
civics.emerged: ~1,900 BCE Old Babylonian rabianum (village mayor) and city elders answering to the palace

capabilities: A head chosen in the village or city ward answers to the palace for its dues, labour levies and crimes, and speaks for it before officials.

civics.name: Ration distribution
civics.desc: Temple and palace issue standard monthly rations of barley, oil and wool to workers, widows and orphans on their lists.
civics.emerged: ~3,100 BCE Uruk bevelled-rim ration bowls; ~2,100 BCE Ur III ration lists

capabilities: Temple and palace issue standard monthly rations of barley, oil and wool to workers, widows and orphans on their lists.

civics.name: Royal storehouses
civics.desc: Revenue in grain, wine and silver is held in sealed provincial storehouses and paid out only by written order, keeping years of reserves.
civics.emerged: ~509-493 BCE Persepolis Fortification tablets (Achaemenid stores and disbursements)

capabilities: Revenue in grain, wine and silver is held in sealed provincial storehouses and paid out only by written order, keeping years of reserves.

civics.name: Ethical religion
civics.desc: Prophets teach that the gods demand justice for the poor rather than sacrifice alone, and judge kings and the rich by that standard.
civics.emerged: ~750 BCE Amos and the Hebrew prophets; ~600 BCE Zoroastrian teaching (dates debated)

capabilities: Prophets teach that the gods demand justice for the poor rather than sacrifice alone, and judge kings and the rich by that standard.

civics.name: Pilgrimage and sacred truce
civics.desc: Sanctuaries draw pilgrims from many states; a sacred truce protects travellers on the roads to the festival.
civics.emerged: ~776 BCE Olympic sacred truce (ekecheiria); ~700 BCE pilgrims to the oracle at Delphi

capabilities: Sanctuaries draw pilgrims from many states; a sacred truce protects travellers on the roads to the festival.

future.system: Society - religion and pilgrimage
future.description: pilgrims travel to shared sanctuaries under a sacred truce

civics.name: Private banking houses
civics.desc: Family firms take deposits, pay on written orders and lend against land, linking farmers, merchants and the treasury.
civics.emerged: ~600 BCE Egibi house of Babylon takes deposits and makes loans; ~440 BCE Murashu house finances tenants

capabilities: Family firms take deposits, pay on written orders and lend against land, linking farmers, merchants and the treasury.

civics.name: Letter schools
civics.desc: Fee-paying teachers teach citizens' children reading, writing and music in small schools.
civics.emerged: ~494 BCE school at Chios (Herodotus); ~480 BCE Athenian school scenes on pottery

capabilities: Fee-paying teachers teach citizens' children reading, writing and music in small schools.

civics.name: Water-turn shares
civics.desc: Those who dig a channel own its flow in timed turns that can be inherited or sold, so new channels are dug.
civics.emerged: ~500 BCE Achaemenid kings grant qanat water to its builders for five generations (Polybius)

capabilities: Those who dig a channel own its flow in timed turns that can be inherited or sold, so new channels are dug.

civics.name: State resettlement
civics.desc: The state moves whole communities from conquered lands to new provinces to farm empty land and break old loyalties.
civics.emerged: ~745 BCE Tiglath-Pileser III resettles conquered peoples; ~587 BCE Babylonian exile

capabilities: The state moves whole communities from conquered lands to new provinces to farm empty land and break old loyalties.

civics.name: Weekly rest day
civics.desc: One day in seven, servants, hired workers and draught animals are released from work by law.
civics.emerged: ~600 BCE Deuteronomic law extends sabbath rest to servants and hired workers

capabilities: One day in seven, servants, hired workers and draught animals are released from work by law.

civics.name: Succession oaths
civics.desc: Officials and vassal kings swear in the old ruler's lifetime to support his chosen heir, under curses if they break the oath.
civics.emerged: 672 BCE Esarhaddon's succession treaties binding vassals and officials to Ashurbanipal

capabilities: Officials and vassal kings swear in the old ruler's lifetime to support his chosen heir, under curses if they break the oath.

civics.name: Siege and road engineers
civics.desc: Specialist troops build ramps, bridges and tracks for the army, and their skills are turned to roads in peace.
civics.emerged: ~865 BCE Assyrian sappers, ramps and river crossings in Ashurnasirpal II's reliefs

capabilities: Specialist troops build ramps, bridges and tracks for the army, and their skills are turned to roads in peace.

civics.name: Tyranny
civics.desc: A strongman seizes a city outside the traditional order, backed by the people or hired troops, and rules through patronage and public works.
civics.emerged: ~657 BCE Cypselus at Corinth; ~546 BCE Peisistratus at Athens

capabilities: A strongman seizes a city outside the traditional order, backed by the people or hired troops, and rules through patronage and public works.

civics.name: Property classes
civics.desc: Citizens are ranked by assessed wealth instead of birth; a family that grows rich can climb into the classes that may hold office.
civics.emerged: ~594 BCE Solon's four property classes at Athens; ~550 BCE Servian classes at Rome (traditional)

capabilities: Citizens are ranked by assessed wealth instead of birth; a family that grows rich can climb into the classes that may hold office.

civics.name: Palace library
civics.desc: The palace collects and catalogues copies of scholarly, religious and medical texts from across the realm.
civics.emerged: ~650 BCE Ashurbanipal's library at Nineveh

capabilities: The palace collects and catalogues copies of scholarly, religious and medical texts from across the realm.

civics.name: Household registers
civics.desc: Every household is entered on a standing register kept by county officials, updated for births, deaths and moves; groups of five answer for each other's dues.
civics.emerged: ~375 BCE Qin registration of households in groups of five; 2 CE Han population register

capabilities: Every household is entered on a standing register kept by county officials, updated for births, deaths and moves; groups of five answer for each other's dues.

civics.name: Congregations
civics.desc: Lay believers meet weekly to hear scripture, share a meal and support their poor, sick and widows from a common fund.
civics.emerged: ~250 BCE synagogue inscriptions in Egypt; ~50 CE Christian assemblies; Buddhist lay observance days

capabilities: Lay believers meet weekly to hear scripture, share a meal and support their poor, sick and widows from a common fund.

civics.name: Hegemonic leagues
civics.desc: Allied cities swear to a common league led by the strongest, paying into a shared treasury for a common fleet or army.
civics.emerged: ~478 BCE Delian League; ~338 BCE League of Corinth

capabilities: Allied cities swear to a common league led by the strongest, paying into a shared treasury for a common fleet or army.

civics.name: Sea loans
civics.desc: Lenders advance money on a ship and cargo, repayable only if the voyage succeeds, so the merchant does not bear the risk of loss alone.
civics.emerged: ~400 BCE Athenian bottomry loans repayable only if the ship returns

capabilities: Lenders advance money on a ship and cargo, repayable only if the voyage succeeds, so the merchant does not bear the risk of loss alone.

civics.name: Rhetoric schools
civics.desc: Paid teachers train young men to argue in courts and assemblies, the path to a public career.
civics.emerged: ~390 BCE Isocrates' school at Athens; ~92 BCE Latin rhetors at Rome

capabilities: Paid teachers train young men to argue in courts and assemblies, the path to a public career.

civics.name: Water commissioners
civics.desc: A permanent office maintains the aqueducts, licenses private connections and punishes theft of water.
civics.emerged: ~11 BCE Roman cura aquarum; ~97 CE Frontinus' De aquaeductu

capabilities: A permanent office maintains the aqueducts, licenses private connections and punishes theft of water.

civics.name: Veteran colonies
civics.desc: Discharged soldiers receive surveyed plots in new or conquered land, founding colonies loyal to the state.
civics.emerged: ~300 BCE Ptolemaic cleruchs in the Fayum; ~100 BCE Roman colonies of discharged legionaries

capabilities: Discharged soldiers receive surveyed plots in new or conquered land, founding colonies loyal to the state.

civics.name: Extended citizenship
civics.desc: Citizenship is granted to allies, freedmen and whole towns; new citizens may marry, trade, sue and settle anywhere under the common law.
civics.emerged: ~338 BCE Roman grants of citizenship to Latin towns; 212 CE Constitutio Antoniniana

capabilities: Citizenship is granted to allies, freedmen and whole towns; new citizens may marry, trade, sue and settle anywhere under the common law.

civics.name: Adoptive succession
civics.desc: The ruler adopts the ablest candidate as his son and heir, giving merit the form of dynastic succession.
civics.emerged: 96–180 CE Nerva–Antonine adoptive emperors

capabilities: The ruler adopts the ablest candidate as his son and heir, giving merit the form of dynastic succession.

civics.name: Ruler cult
civics.desc: Provinces raise temples and priests to the living or deified ruler; local notables compete to hold the priesthood, binding them to the empire.
civics.emerged: ~300 BCE Hellenistic ruler cults; 29 BCE first provincial temples to Augustus

capabilities: Provinces raise temples and priests to the living or deified ruler; local notables compete to hold the priesthood, binding them to the empire.

civics.name: Military treatises
civics.desc: Commanders write down doctrine on scouting, spies, supply and terrain, and officers study it.
civics.emerged: ~500 BCE Sunzi's Art of War; ~350 BCE Aeneas Tacticus

capabilities: Commanders write down doctrine on scouting, spies, supply and terrain, and officers study it.

civics.name: Public physicians
civics.desc: The city pays a salaried physician to treat its citizens, rich and poor alike.
civics.emerged: ~525 BCE Democedes paid as public physician by Aegina and Athens (Herodotus)

capabilities: The city pays a salaried physician to treat its citizens, rich and poor alike.

civics.name: Selection by lot
civics.desc: Many offices are filled by drawing lots among eligible citizens, so no faction can buy or monopolize them and every citizen may serve.
civics.emerged: ~487 BCE Athenian archons chosen by lot; ~462 BCE allotted jury panels

capabilities: Many offices are filled by drawing lots among eligible citizens, so no faction can buy or monopolize them and every citizen may serve.

civics.name: Child-support foundations
civics.desc: Endowed funds pay a monthly allowance to poor children in each town, financed by interest on loans to local landowners.
civics.emerged: ~97 CE Nerva's and Trajan's alimenta for freeborn children in Italian towns

capabilities: Endowed funds pay a monthly allowance to poor children in each town, financed by interest on loans to local landowners.

civics.name: Agronomic treatises
civics.desc: Landowners write and read manuals on crops, soils, manuring and estate management.
civics.emerged: ~160 BCE Cato's On Agriculture; ~20 BCE Fan Shengzhi's farming manual
civics.prereq: scribal_schools AND (alphabet_vowels OR chinese_script OR abjad)

capabilities: Landowners write and read manuals on crops, soils, manuring and estate management.

civics.name: Chancery enrolment
civics.desc: Copies of every letter and writ sent out are entered on rolls, so the government knows what it has granted and ordered and can enforce it.
civics.emerged: ~1,199 CE English chancery rolls of outgoing letters and writs

capabilities: Copies of every letter and writ sent out are entered on rolls, so the government knows what it has granted and ordered and can enforce it.

civics.name: Exchequer audit
civics.desc: Sheriffs account twice a year at a chequered counting table; sums owed and paid are written on rolls, and arrears follow the official until cleared.
civics.emerged: ~1,110 CE English Exchequer; 1,130 CE first surviving pipe roll

capabilities: Sheriffs account twice a year at a chequered counting table; sums owed and paid are written on rolls, and arrears follow the official until cleared.

civics.name: Parish tithe
civics.desc: Every household owes a tenth of its grain and young stock to its parish church. The tenth is gathered in the tithe barn to keep the clergy, the church and the parish poor.
civics.emerged: 779 CE Capitulary of Herstal makes the tithe compulsory across the Frankish realm; tithe barns built across Europe from ~1,100 CE

capabilities: Every household owes a tenth of its grain and young stock to its parish church. The tenth is gathered in the tithe barn to keep the clergy, the church and the parish poor.

civics.name: Vernacular literature
civics.desc: Poets and storytellers write in the spoken tongue for lay readers rather than in the learned language.
civics.emerged: ~1,008 CE The Tale of Genji; ~1,320 CE Dante's Commedia

capabilities: Poets and storytellers write in the spoken tongue for lay readers rather than in the learned language.

civics.name: Holy war
civics.desc: War against unbelievers is declared a religious duty with spiritual rewards, and conquered frontier land is settled by the faithful.
civics.emerged: ~750 CE jihad doctrine in early Islamic law; 1095 CE First Crusade preached

capabilities: War against unbelievers is declared a religious duty with spiritual rewards, and conquered frontier land is settled by the faithful.

civics.name: Church-state concordat
civics.desc: Church and crown divide authority over bishops: the church confers spiritual office, the ruler the lands, ending wars over who appoints them.
civics.emerged: 1107 CE Concordat of London; 1122 CE Concordat of Worms

capabilities: Church and crown divide authority over bishops: the church confers spiritual office, the ruler the lands, ending wars over who appoints them.

civics.name: Mendicant friars
civics.desc: Friars without property preach and beg in the towns, nursing the sick and serving the urban poor.
civics.emerged: 1209 CE Franciscan rule; 1216 CE Dominican order

capabilities: Friars without property preach and beg in the towns, nursing the sick and serving the urban poor.

civics.name: Peace of God
civics.desc: Church councils forbid knights to attack peasants, clergy, mills or oxen, and ban fighting on holy days, enforcing it with excommunication and sworn peace leagues.
civics.emerged: 989 CE Council of Charroux; 1,027 CE Truce of God at Toulouges: bishops forbid violence against peasants, clergy and their goods on pain of excommunication

capabilities: Church councils forbid knights to attack peasants, clergy, mills or oxen, and ban fighting on holy days, enforcing it with excommunication and sworn peace leagues.

civics.name: Safe-conduct
civics.desc: A ruler's written guarantee protects named foreigners, their goods and their servants while they travel in his land.
civics.emerged: ~650 CE aman granted to foreign envoys and merchants; ~1,414 CE English Safe Conducts Act

capabilities: A ruler's written guarantee protects named foreigners, their goods and their servants while they travel in his land.

civics.name: Commenda partnership
civics.desc: A stay-at-home investor funds a travelling merchant for one voyage and they split the profit, so a young trader without capital can start out.
civics.emerged: ~800 CE Islamic qirad contracts; ~1,072 CE Venetian colleganza

capabilities: A stay-at-home investor funds a travelling merchant for one voyage and they split the profit, so a young trader without capital can start out.

civics.name: Cathedral and madrasa schools
civics.desc: Endowed schools at cathedrals and mosques teach grammar, law and theology to boys who will become clergy, judges and clerks.
civics.emerged: ~1,067 CE Nizamiyya madrasa, Baghdad; ~1,079 CE papal decree requiring cathedral schools

capabilities: Endowed schools at cathedrals and mosques teach grammar, law and theology to boys who will become clergy, judges and clerks.

civics.name: Bridge trusts
civics.desc: Brotherhoods and endowed trusts raise alms, rents and bequests to build stone bridges and keep them in repair forever, with wardens who answer for the fund.
civics.emerged: ~1,177 CE Pont Saint-Bénézet, Avignon, built by a bridge brotherhood; 1,282 CE London Bridge House estate; 1,399 CE Rochester Bridge Trust

capabilities: Brotherhoods and endowed trusts raise alms, rents and bequests to build stone bridges and keep them in repair forever, with wardens who answer for the fund.

civics.name: Water boards
civics.desc: Landholders elect a board that levies a rate, keeps the dikes and drains the polders.
civics.emerged: ~1,255 CE Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland: landholders govern dikes and drainage

capabilities: Landholders elect a board that levies a rate, keeps the dikes and drains the polders.

civics.name: Marcher lordships
civics.desc: Frontier districts are granted to lords with wide powers to raise troops, build castles and push the border outward.
civics.emerged: ~795 CE Carolingian Spanish March; ~1,070 CE Welsh Marches

capabilities: Frontier districts are granted to lords with wide powers to raise troops, build castles and push the border outward.

civics.name: Printed classics
civics.desc: The state prints authorized editions of the classics and sells them cheaply to schools and examination candidates.
civics.emerged: ~932 CE Feng Dao begins state printing of the Confucian classics (completed 953 CE)

capabilities: The state prints authorized editions of the classics and sells them cheaply to schools and examination candidates.

civics.name: Apprenticeship indentures
civics.desc: A written indenture binds a youth to a master for years of training in return for board and the right to become a journeyman.
civics.emerged: ~1,268 CE Paris Livre des métiers fixes apprenticeship terms

capabilities: A written indenture binds a youth to a master for years of training in return for board and the right to become a journeyman.

civics.name: Sharecropping contracts
civics.desc: A landowner provides land, seed and plough oxen; a free tenant family provides labour, and the harvest is split by agreed shares.
civics.emerged: ~800 CE muzāraʿa and musāqāt sharecropping contracts in the Islamic law books; ~1,250 CE Tuscan mezzadria

capabilities: A landowner provides land, seed and plough oxen; a free tenant family provides labour, and the harvest is split by agreed shares.

civics.name: Courts of appeal
civics.desc: A higher court reviews the judgments of local judges and petitions against officials; a wrong verdict can be overturned without bribing the governor.
civics.emerged: ~800 CE Abbasid mazalim courts hearing complaints against officials; ~1,250 CE Parlement of Paris

capabilities: A higher court reviews the judgments of local judges and petitions against officials; a wrong verdict can be overturned without bribing the governor.

civics.name: Public notaries
civics.desc: Licensed notaries draw up contracts, wills and sales in set forms and keep registers; a notarial deed is proof in any court.
civics.emerged: ~1,154 CE Genoese notarial cartulary (Giovanni Scriba); ~1,255 CE Rolandino's Summa artis notariae (Bologna)

capabilities: Licensed notaries draw up contracts, wills and sales in set forms and keep registers; a notarial deed is proof in any court.

civics.name: Primogeniture
civics.desc: The eldest son inherits the realm or fief undivided; younger sons go to the church, the army or abroad.
civics.emerged: ~1,000 CE Capetian succession of eldest sons; ~1,100 CE indivisible fiefs in Normandy and England

capabilities: The eldest son inherits the realm or fief undivided; younger sons go to the church, the army or abroad.

civics.name: Slave-soldier corps
civics.desc: The ruler buys or levies boys from outside, trains them as soldiers, and promotes the able to command and governorships.
civics.emerged: ~833 CE al-Mu'tasim's Turkic ghulam guard; ~1,380 CE Ottoman Janissaries

capabilities: The ruler buys or levies boys from outside, trains them as soldiers, and promotes the able to command and governorships.

civics.name: Hospitals
civics.desc: Endowed hospitals with wards, physicians and pharmacies take in the sick without charge.
civics.emerged: ~805 CE Baghdad bimaristan; ~1,136 CE Pantokrator hospital, Constantinople

capabilities: Endowed hospitals with wards, physicians and pharmacies take in the sick without charge.

civics.name: Caliphate
civics.desc: The successor of the Prophet leads the community of believers in war, law and taxation, through governors and a register of revenues.
civics.emerged: 632 CE Rashidun caliphate; 750 CE Abbasid caliphate

capabilities: The successor of the Prophet leads the community of believers in war, law and taxation, through governors and a register of revenues.

civics.name: Village by-laws
civics.desc: The village meeting sets the dates of ploughing, harvest and gleaning and the number of beasts on the common, and fines those who break the rules.
civics.emerged: ~1,270 CE English manorial by-laws on harvest and grazing; ~1,300 CE Landsgemeinde of the Swiss forest cantons

capabilities: The village meeting sets the dates of ploughing, harvest and gleaning and the number of beasts on the common, and fines those who break the rules.

civics.name: Mutual-aid fraternities
civics.desc: Members pay regular dues into a common box that supports them when sick and pays for their burial.
civics.emerged: ~1,200 CE guild and parish fraternities fund sick members and burials

capabilities: Members pay regular dues into a common box that supports them when sick and pays for their burial.

civics.name: Chartered universities
civics.desc: Masters and students form self-governing corporations with charters, faculties and degrees recognized across realms.
civics.emerged: ~1,088 CE Bologna; ~1,150 CE Paris masters' guild

capabilities: Masters and students form self-governing corporations with charters, faculties and degrees recognized across realms.

civics.name: Geographic compendia
civics.desc: Scholars compile travellers' and merchants' reports into world descriptions with maps and itineraries.
civics.emerged: ~1,154 CE al-Idrisi's Tabula Rogeriana; ~1,225 CE Zhao Rugua's Records of Foreign Peoples

capabilities: Scholars compile travellers' and merchants' reports into world descriptions with maps and itineraries.

civics.name: Patronage of translation
civics.desc: Patrons pay scholars to translate the science and philosophy of other languages and copy the translations widely.
civics.emerged: ~830 CE House of Wisdom, Baghdad; ~1,150 CE Toledo translators

capabilities: Patrons pay scholars to translate the science and philosophy of other languages and copy the translations widely.

civics.name: Intendants
civics.desc: Royal commissioners, removable at will and paid by the crown, oversee justice, police and finance in each province and report by post to the council.
civics.emerged: ~1,635 CE French intendants made permanent under Richelieu

capabilities: Royal commissioners, removable at will and paid by the crown, oversee justice, police and finance in each province and report by post to the council.

civics.name: Confessional state
civics.desc: Each ruler fixes his territory's confession; the church keeps parish registers of births, marriages and deaths and disciplines the parish.
civics.emerged: 1555 CE Peace of Augsburg; 1563 CE Tridentine parish registers

capabilities: Each ruler fixes his territory's confession; the church keeps parish registers of births, marriages and deaths and disciplines the parish.

civics.name: Revival movements
civics.desc: Lay devotional circles call for personal conversion and good works, founding orphanages, charity schools and Bible societies.
civics.emerged: ~1,690 CE German Pietism and the Halle foundations; ~1,735 CE Great Awakening

capabilities: Lay devotional circles call for personal conversion and good works, founding orphanages, charity schools and Bible societies.

civics.name: Insurance underwriting
civics.desc: Underwriters take a share of a ship's or a life's risk for a premium priced on recorded losses.
civics.emerged: ~1,688 CE Lloyd's coffee-house underwriters; ~1,693 CE Halley's life table

capabilities: Underwriters take a share of a ship's or a life's risk for a premium priced on recorded losses.

civics.name: Humanist colleges
civics.desc: Colleges teach graded classes of boys Latin, Greek, rhetoric and history from printed textbooks.
civics.emerged: ~1,538 CE Sturm's Strasbourg Gymnasium; ~1,548 CE Jesuit college at Messina

capabilities: Colleges teach graded classes of boys Latin, Greek, rhetoric and history from printed textbooks.

civics.name: Organised fire-fighting
civics.desc: Towns keep engines, hoses and trained crews ready to answer any fire.
civics.emerged: ~1,672 CE Amsterdam fire-hose brigades; ~1,680 CE London Fire Office

capabilities: Towns keep engines, hoses and trained crews ready to answer any fire.

civics.name: Turnpike trusts
civics.desc: Trusts collect tolls from road users and spend them on resurfacing and straightening the highway.
civics.emerged: ~1,663 CE first English turnpike act; ~1,706 CE turnpike trusts

capabilities: Trusts collect tolls from road users and spend them on resurfacing and straightening the highway.

civics.name: Reason of state
civics.desc: The interest of the state is placed above religious and dynastic claims: rulers build revenue, armies and alliances for the state's sake.
civics.emerged: 1589 CE Botero, Della ragion di stato; ~1,630 CE Richelieu's policy

capabilities: The interest of the state is placed above religious and dynastic claims: rulers build revenue, armies and alliances for the state's sake.

civics.name: Printed newspapers
civics.desc: Printers issue weekly sheets of news and merchants' price currents gathered from the posts.
civics.emerged: ~1,605 CE Strasbourg Relation; ~1,618 CE Amsterdam Courante

capabilities: Printers issue weekly sheets of news and merchants' price currents gathered from the posts.

civics.name: Bankruptcy law
civics.desc: When a trader fails, his goods are gathered and shared among creditors by rule, and an honest debtor can be discharged and trade again.
civics.emerged: ~1,542 CE English Statute of Bankrupts; 1,705 CE discharge of honest bankrupts (England)

capabilities: When a trader fails, his goods are gathered and shared among creditors by rule, and an honest debtor can be discharged and trade again.

civics.name: Army magazines
civics.desc: The state keeps grain magazines for the army along the frontier and opens them to the public in famine years.
civics.emerged: ~1,670 CE Louvois's magazine system; ~1,771 CE Prussian magazines opened for famine relief

capabilities: The state keeps grain magazines for the army along the frontier and opens them to the public in famine years.

civics.name: Corps of engineers
civics.desc: A permanent corps of trained engineers designs fortresses, bridges and roads and surveys the ground.
civics.emerged: ~1,690 CE Vauban's corps of engineers; ~1,716 CE French Corps des ponts et chaussées

capabilities: A permanent corps of trained engineers designs fortresses, bridges and roads and surveys the ground.

civics.name: Language academies
civics.desc: Chartered academies fix the standard language in an official dictionary and grammar.
civics.emerged: ~1,582 CE Accademia della Crusca; ~1,635 CE Académie française

capabilities: Chartered academies fix the standard language in an official dictionary and grammar.

civics.name: Civil registration
civics.desc: Every birth, marriage and death is recorded by a public registrar; each person has a legal identity, and the state sees where infants are dying.
civics.emerged: 1,792 CE French etat civil; 1,837 CE General Register Office (England and Wales)

capabilities: Every birth, marriage and death is recorded by a public registrar; each person has a legal identity, and the state sees where infants are dying.

civics.name: Abolition of internal tolls
civics.desc: Tolls at provincial borders, rivers and town gates are abolished; duties are collected once, at the national frontier, by one customs service.
civics.emerged: 1,790 CE abolition of internal customs in France; 1,818 CE Prussian customs law

capabilities: Tolls at provincial borders, rivers and town gates are abolished; duties are collected once, at the national frontier, by one customs service.

civics.name: Prefects
civics.desc: Each uniform department is run by a prefect appointed by and answering to the interior ministry, applying the same laws, levies and conscription everywhere.
civics.emerged: 1,800 CE French prefects (law of 28 Pluviose year VIII)

capabilities: Each uniform department is run by a prefect appointed by and answering to the interior ministry, applying the same laws, levies and conscription everywhere.

civics.name: Industrial exhibitions
civics.desc: Great halls display the newest machines, crops and manufactures to millions of visitors and juries award prizes.
civics.emerged: ~1,851 CE Great Exhibition, London

capabilities: Great halls display the newest machines, crops and manufactures to millions of visitors and juries award prizes.

civics.name: National literature
civics.desc: Scholars collect folk tales and songs and print them as the nation's own literature, taught in schools.
civics.emerged: ~1,812 CE Grimms' Children's and Household Tales; ~1,835 CE Kalevala

capabilities: Scholars collect folk tales and songs and print them as the nation's own literature, taught in schools.

civics.name: Missionary societies
civics.desc: Voluntary societies fund missionaries abroad, who found schools and clinics and send home reports and maps of the interior.
civics.emerged: 1792 CE Baptist Missionary Society; 1795 CE London Missionary Society

capabilities: Voluntary societies fund missionaries abroad, who found schools and clinics and send home reports and maps of the interior.

civics.name: Social Christianity
civics.desc: Churches take up the labour question, backing fair wages, workers' associations, settlement houses and relief for the industrial poor.
civics.emerged: 1848 CE Christian socialists in London; ~1,880 CE Social Gospel; 1891 CE Rerum Novarum

capabilities: Churches take up the labour question, backing fair wages, workers' associations, settlement houses and relief for the industrial poor.

civics.name: Consular service
civics.desc: Salaried state consuls in foreign ports protect nationals and report on markets, prices and shipping.
civics.emerged: ~1,825 CE British Consular Act; ~1,856 CE US consular reform

capabilities: Salaried state consuls in foreign ports protect nationals and report on markets, prices and shipping.

civics.name: River commissions
civics.desc: States along a river set common rules, tolls and channel works under a standing commission so ships move freely.
civics.emerged: ~1,815 CE Central Commission for Navigation on the Rhine; ~1,856 CE European Danube Commission

capabilities: States along a river set common rules, tolls and channel works under a standing commission so ships move freely.

civics.name: Commodity exchange
civics.desc: Graded grain and cotton are traded for present and future delivery on a regulated exchange.
civics.emerged: ~1,848 CE Chicago Board of Trade; ~1,865 CE standardised grain futures

capabilities: Graded grain and cotton are traded for present and future delivery on a regulated exchange.

civics.name: Agricultural colleges
civics.desc: Colleges teach scientific farming, run experimental fields and train estate managers and farmers' sons.
civics.emerged: ~1,818 CE Hohenheim agricultural academy; ~1,862 CE Morrill Land-Grant Act

capabilities: Colleges teach scientific farming, run experimental fields and train estate managers and farmers' sons.

civics.name: Medical education reform
civics.desc: Medical schools are tied to universities and teaching hospitals, with laboratory science and clinical training required.
civics.emerged: ~1,893 CE Johns Hopkins School of Medicine; ~1,910 CE Flexner Report

capabilities: Medical schools are tied to universities and teaching hospitals, with laboratory science and clinical training required.

civics.name: Normal schools
civics.desc: Teacher-training colleges prepare elementary teachers in subject and method to a common standard.
civics.emerged: ~1,794 CE Paris École normale; ~1,839 CE Lexington normal school

capabilities: Teacher-training colleges prepare elementary teachers in subject and method to a common standard.

civics.name: Mining and technical academies
civics.desc: State academies train engineers and mine officials in chemistry, mechanics and geology.
civics.emerged: ~1,765 CE Freiberg Mining Academy; ~1,794 CE École polytechnique

capabilities: State academies train engineers and mine officials in chemistry, mechanics and geology.

civics.name: Women's higher education
civics.desc: Colleges and secondary schools open to women and girls, and women begin to take degrees and enter the professions.
civics.emerged: ~1,869 CE Girton College; ~1,880 CE Camille Sée law founding girls' lycées

capabilities: Colleges and secondary schools open to women and girls, and women begin to take degrees and enter the professions.

civics.name: Housing reform acts

civics.emerged: ~1,875 CE Artisans' Dwellings Act; ~1,890 CE Housing of the Working Classes Act

capabilities: Councils may condemn unfit slums and require new dwellings to meet standards of light, drainage and soundness.

civics.name: Municipal waterworks
civics.desc: The city builds and runs its own filtered water supply and sewers for every street.
civics.emerged: ~1,842 CE Croton Aqueduct, New York; ~1,859 CE London main drainage

capabilities: The city builds and runs its own filtered water supply and sewers for every street.

civics.name: Assisted emigration
civics.desc: Colonies pay the passage of chosen emigrants from land-sale revenue so labourers can reach distant colonies.
civics.emerged: ~1,831 CE assisted passages to New South Wales; ~1,840 CE Colonial Land and Emigration Commission

capabilities: Colonies pay the passage of chosen emigrants from land-sale revenue so labourers can reach distant colonies.

civics.name: Coaling stations
civics.desc: The navy holds a chain of ports stocked with coal so steam ships can cross oceans.

capabilities: The navy holds a chain of ports stocked with coal so steam ships can cross oceans.

civics.name: Geographical societies
civics.desc: Learned societies fund expeditions, publish maps and train explorers in survey.
civics.emerged: ~1,821 CE Société de Géographie; ~1,830 CE Royal Geographical Society

capabilities: Learned societies fund expeditions, publish maps and train explorers in survey.

civics.name: Colonial self-government

capabilities: Settler colonies gain their own cabinet answerable to an elected assembly, while foreign affairs stay with the empire.

civics.name: New imperialism

civics.emerged: ~1,870 CE civilizing-mission doctrine; 1884–1885 CE Berlin Conference

capabilities: Overseas empire is argued to be a national necessity and a civilizing mission; colonies are claimed and settled by agreement among powers.

civics.name: Progressivism
civics.desc: Reformers use investigative journalism, experts and regulation to clean up cities, food, factories and politics.
civics.emerged: ~1,890 CE US Progressive movement; 1906 CE Pure Food and Drug Act

capabilities: Reformers use investigative journalism, experts and regulation to clean up cities, food, factories and politics.

civics.name: Social democracy

civics.emerged: 1875 CE Gotha programme; 1891 CE Erfurt programme; 1899 CE Bernstein's revisionism

capabilities: Socialist parties seek reform through elections and parliament: social insurance, labour law and public services instead of revolution.

civics.name: Advertising

civics.emerged: ~1,841 CE Volney Palmer's advertising agency, Philadelphia

capabilities: Agencies buy space in the papers and write notices that tell buyers what is for sale, where and at what price.

civics.name: Telegraph news agencies

civics.emerged: ~1,849 CE Wolff's telegraphic bureau; ~1,851 CE Reuters

capabilities: Agencies gather news and market prices by telegraph and sell them to every paper at once.

civics.name: Industrial arbitration

civics.emerged: ~1,894 CE New Zealand Industrial Conciliation and Arbitration Act; ~1,896 CE UK Conciliation Act

capabilities: Disputes between unions and employers go to a conciliation board or arbitration court instead of a strike.

civics.name: Labour exchanges
civics.desc: Public offices list vacancies and job-seekers and match them across the country.
civics.emerged: ~1,894 CE German municipal labour exchanges; ~1,909 CE UK Labour Exchanges Act

capabilities: Public offices list vacancies and job-seekers and match them across the country.

civics.name: Minimum wage

civics.emerged: ~1,896 CE Victoria wages boards; ~1,909 CE UK Trade Boards Act

capabilities: Wage boards set a legal floor under the pay of the lowest-paid trades.

civics.name: Workmen's compensation

civics.emerged: ~1,884 CE German accident insurance; ~1,897 CE UK Workmen's Compensation Act

capabilities: Employers must compensate workers injured on the job, whoever was at fault.

civics.name: Administrative courts

civics.emerged: 1,799 CE French Conseil d'Etat; 1,872 CE its independent jurisdiction

capabilities: Citizens can sue the administration before specialist judges; officials who exceed their powers see their acts annulled, so every province is run by the same rules.

civics.name: Married women's property

civics.emerged: 1,839 CE Mississippi Married Women's Property Act; 1,882 CE English Married Women's Property Act

capabilities: A wife keeps her own earnings, property and inheritance and may contract and sue in her own name, so women can run shops and enter trades.

civics.name: Penitentiaries

civics.emerged: 1,790 CE Walnut Street Jail (Philadelphia); 1,842 CE Pentonville prison (London)

capabilities: Prison terms graded by offence replace branding, flogging and the gallows for most crimes; convicts are held, worked and released rather than maimed or killed.

civics.name: Trademark law

civics.emerged: 1,857 CE French trademark law; 1,875 CE UK Trade Marks Registration Act

capabilities: Makers register their marks and copying one is a wrong, so buyers far away can trust a branded sack of flour or tin of tea.

civics.name: Civic ritual

civics.emerged: 1790 CE Fête de la Fédération; 1795 CE La Marseillaise adopted; 1880 CE Bastille Day

capabilities: Flags, anthems, national holidays and monuments give the sovereign nation its own rites, celebrated in every town.

capabilities: A ruler seeks the people's direct approval in a yes-or-no vote on his rule or constitution, bypassing representatives.

civics.name: Colonial regiments

civics.emerged: ~1,757 CE East India Company sepoy battalions; ~1,857 CE Tirailleurs sénégalais

capabilities: The colonial government raises regiments from local recruits under contract to garrison and police its territories.

capabilities: The law requires every infant to be vaccinated against smallpox and records each vaccination.

capabilities: An emperor rules with authoritarian powers confirmed by plebiscites, through prefects, a mass army and public works.

capabilities: Ratepayers elect a town council with a budget of its own; it paves, lights and drains streets and maintains the roads of its district.

capabilities: Elected district councils of landowners, townsmen and peasants run rural schools, clinics, roads and grain reserves for relief in bad years.

capabilities: Wage-earners pay weekly into registered societies that pay benefit in sickness, old age and death.

capabilities: The law requires workers and employers to pay into funds that cover sickness, accident and old age.

capabilities: Towns fund free lending libraries and reading rooms open to every resident.

civics.name: Customs modernization

capabilities: States fund institutes abroad that teach their language and present their culture.

capabilities: Studios make feature films shown in thousands of cinemas to mass weekly audiences.

civics.name: Modernist design

capabilities: Designers and architects plan compact, standardized dwellings and furniture for mass housing.

capabilities: Clergy and lay base communities read scripture as a call to free the poor, organizing cooperatives, soup kitchens and land claims.

capabilities: Mass movements seek to order state and society by religious values, combining preaching, welfare networks and electoral politics.

civics.name: Academic exchange

civics.emerged: ~1,946 CE Fulbright Program; ~1,987 CE Erasmus Programme

capabilities: Governments fund students and scholars to study and teach abroad.

civics.name: Civil aviation agreements

capabilities: States agree rights to fly over and land in each other's territory and common air safety rules.

capabilities: International banks lend to governments for roads, dams and power plants.

capabilities: Surplus food is shipped through international programmes to countries in famine.

capabilities: Currencies are pegged to an agreed standard and defended by central banks with a shared reserve fund.

capabilities: Small loans are made to groups of poor borrowers who guarantee each other, without collateral.

capabilities: The state buys surplus grain at a guaranteed price and holds it in reserve stocks.

capabilities: Designated districts offer foreign firms low tariffs, light regulation and ready sites, drawing industry and workers.

capabilities: Adults study for degrees at home through broadcast lectures, post and later the internet.

capabilities: Public grants and new campuses open university study to a large share of each generation.

capabilities: Every child stays at school into the teens, in free state secondary schools.

capabilities: Coastal states set catch quotas in their waters to let fish stocks recover.

civics.name: National highway programmes

capabilities: Independent institutes employ researchers to analyse public policy and propose reforms to governments and parties.

civics.name: Institutional reform
civics.desc: Repeated, evidence-led reform of the administrative machinery: audits, reorganizations and the retirement of offices that no longer serve. Each level extends how far the centre's authority reaches before it decays. A repeatable civic: available only once every finite civic of the final Age is researched (the end-of-tree safety valve).
civics.emerged: repeatable

capabilities: administrative reach extends further per level

effect.form: each level closes a fixed fraction of the remaining gap to the operand's cap — diminishing, never reaching it (DD-14)
effect.limit: the reach of a perfectly efficient administration

repeatable.law2: coefficient inside a named resolution equation, not a free-floating buff
repeatable.status: DOCUMENTED — the operand is read once the tranche-2 effects engine lands (KnowledgeEffects, LevelContribution seam)
repeatable.engine: LEVELS (ADR-049; D-063 R4) behind tuning.repeatableLevels — off: completes once (D-044 R11); on: each completion raises the level and the node stays available

availability.rule: own prerequisites satisfied AND every finite civic of Age A9 complete (ADR-049; tranche-2 contract §4: the end-of-tree safety valve)

repeatable.benefit_rule: each level closes a fixed fraction k of the remaining gap to the cap: level n adds cap × k(1−k)^(n−1)
repeatable.ui: researched N×, next level cost, per-level and cumulative effect; never marked complete

costRationale.note: repeatable (ADR-049): priced as level 1 on the A9 civic scale; each later level costs ×costGrowth
